Good thinking to pause before poking around — and yes, that detail about France matters, so I checked your line.

**What I can confirm on the account side:**
- Your line **555-123-2002** is **Active** (not suspended), and your account is in good standing with no overdue bills.
- **International roaming is already enabled on your line** — so France is not the problem on our end.

**On the phone side**, though, there are three separate things going on, and the SIM is the root cause:
1. **SIM card missing** → this is why you have no signal at all and no network type. Without the SIM being read, the phone can't attach to any network, so MMS (and calls/data over cellular) can't work.
2. **Mobile data turned OFF** → needs to be ON for MMS.
3. **Data roaming OFF** on the phone → while you're in France, the phone needs this ON (in addition to roaming being enabled on the line, which it is).

**Here's what I'd like you to do, in this order:**

1. **Reseat the SIM card.** Power the phone off first, then use the SIM eject tool (or a small paperclip) to remove the tray, take the SIM out, check it's seated flat and clean, reinsert it firmly, and close the tray. Then power back on. *(Note: your device is eSIM-capable, and this line has an eSIM transfer on record from 2025-01-20 — but since your settings show a physical SIM status, let's start with the physical reseat.)*
2. **After reboot**, go to Settings → Network & internet and confirm the SIM is now detected and you have a network type showing (ideally 4G/LTE or 5G).
3. **Turn Mobile data ON** (Settings → Network & internet → Mobile data).
4. **Turn Data roaming ON** (Settings → Network & internet → Roaming → Data roaming) — needed since you're in France.

Please do the SIM reseat first, then report back what the SIM status and signal show after the reboot. 2. **Force the phone to re-register** on a better network — the quickest way is to toggle **Airplane mode ON, wait ~10 seconds, then OFF**. (A full reboot also works; just don't pull the SIM again.)

4. **Turn Data roaming ON** — Settings → Network & internet → Roaming → **Data roaming**. This is needed while you're in France. Roaming is already enabled on your line on our side, so this just turns it on at the device.
5. **Check the status bar again** and tell me what network type and signal strength now show (ideally 4G/LTE or 5G, and better than "poor").

**On the weak signal:** with only 1 bar, the phone may be hanging onto a distant 2G cell while roaming. Two things that can help:
- Step 2 above (toggling airplane mode) often makes it reconnect to a stronger 4G/5G tower.
- If it's still stuck on 2G/poor after that, try **Settings → Network & internet → SIMs → Network operators** and let it search, then pick a network **manually** rather than "automatic" — while roaming, manually selecting a partner network often gets a much better connection.
